mechanism_narrative: The t-0w rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES from multi-week lows signals a reopening impulse that broadens mobility, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w TRANSIT rose to -25.0 from -31.3 and WORKPLACES rose to -37.3 from -44.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES staying above their t-0w levels.

mechanism_narrative: The one-week jump in GROCERY_PHARM above -20 indicates households are resuming routine errands, which spills over into nearby retail and recreation footfall and lifts RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved to -18.6 at t-0w from -24.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above -20 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening-policy regime, WORKPLACES recovery leads retail recovery because returning commuters restore weekday foot traffic, so RETAIL_REC rises over two weeks when WORKPLACES crosses above -40.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses above -40 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose to -37.3 at t-0w after -44.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES is above -40 for two consecutive weeks under reopening policy but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous fall in RESIDENTIAL below 6 and rise in TRANSIT above -30 means people are replacing staying home with out-of-home trips, which disproportionately increases retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6.0 while TRANSIT rises above -30.0
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w RESIDENTIAL fell to 5.1 and TRANSIT rose to -25.0
failure_condition: If the joint condition RESIDENTIAL < 6.0 and TRANSIT > -30.0 holds for one week but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in WORKPLACES above -38 reflects restored commuting demand that supports weekday retail activity, so RETAIL_REC is higher over the next four weeks after this threshold is crossed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -38 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays above -38 for at least two weeks but RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w RETAIL_REC improvement is a transient seasonal and outdoor-weather effect that fades unless PARKS stays above +8; if PARKS falls back below +6, RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks will be lower than the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below +6 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 9.4 at t-0w but only 5.7 at t-2w
failure_condition: If PARKS falls below +6 but RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remains above +8 while RESIDENTIAL falls below 6, outdoor leisure is drawing people out of home and creates spillover retail trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS > 8 and RESIDENTIAL < 6 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-lockdown reopening regime, simultaneous recovery in GROCERY_PHARM above -20 and TRANSIT above -28 reduces infection-risk caution, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM > -20 and TRANSIT > -28 persist for two weeks in reopening but RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is lower than or equal to last-28-day mean.
